prompt: Implement single-point crossover of two equal-length parent strings: the child takes the first `cut` characters from parent a and the rest from parent b. Complete the cross method in the starter file.
explanation: Crossover is how genetic algorithms combine two parents into a child: a cut point splits both genomes and the child inherits the prefix of one and the suffix of the other. Clamping with Math.max(0, Math.min(cut, len)) protects substring from throwing on out-of-range cut points. substring(0, cut) takes the prefix of a and substring(cut) takes the suffix of b, and string concatenation joins them.
hints: Clamp the cut point first so substring can never throw: it must not drop below 0 nor run past the length of parent a.
a.substring(0, clamped) is the prefix; b.substring(clamped) is the suffix; concatenate them with +.
